info.description: Keeps an AI model catalog (models, the artifacts each is published as, and the inference runtime profiles they run on), registers AI applications as a name, files and a script with versions, deploys an inference service or an application onto nodes CB-Tumblebug already runs through Semaphore, publishes the same capabilities as MCP tools and archives every deploy and control call. Automation engine routes and the partner natural language agent routes are forwarded to their own processes.

post.description: Upload the files of an AI application and the script that deploys it, as one multipart/form-data body. Uploading again under a registered name adds the next version (the highest version plus one); earlier versions are kept. A node receiving a version gets every file in one folder and runs the script from that folder; the target node and the addresses of other nodes are given by the deployment request, not here. File names are the filename of each files part, used as is: one name of letters, digits, ".", "_", "+" and "-", not starting with "." (.env is written by the deployment request), at most 255 characters, each name once. A name with a path such as ../x or conf/x is refused, not shortened. The script is at most 64 KiB, at most 256 files are accepted, and the script and files together may not exceed the upload bound of the service (AIAPP_APP_UPLOAD_MAX_BYTES, 256 MiB by default).

get.description: Report whether the catalog sync is enabled and running, how long it waits between scheduled runs, and how the last run of each configured source went: when it started and finished, how many models the source returned, what they did to the catalog (added, updated, marked stale, skipped because another origin holds the id, dropped as invalid) and the error when the source failed. Before a source has run once only its name is given. With AIAPP_CATALOG_SYNC_ENABLED off, enabled is false and sources is empty.

post.description: Start one run of every configured source in the background and return at once with the status, running true. Poll GET /catalog/sync for the results. The sync adds the models a source lists, updates the ones it added before (keeping runtimes[].verifiedAt), marks stale the ones the source no longer lists and never changes a model of origin seed or manual or of another source. At the end of the run it deletes the models of every source that is not configured in AIAPP_CATALOG_SYNC_SOURCES; seed and manual models are never deleted. Only one run happens at a time: while one is in progress, including the scheduled one, this answers 409.

post.description:
Deploy an inference service or an uploaded AI application onto nodes CB-Tumblebug already runs. This service does not create VMs.

type inference needs inference: modelId and artifactId from GET /models, and optionally runtimeId (a runtime profile from GET /runtimes the artifact lists; defaults to its first), gpu and args (extra runtime arguments appended after the ones the service sets and the catalog args of the artifact, runtimes[].args, which a repeated flag here overrides for vllm, such as ["--max-model-len","32768"] for vllm; at most 32, each 1 to 256 characters without control characters, never --model, --port or --host; ollama refuses them). A docker-compose.yml is rendered from the artifact and the runtime profile (preview it with GET /models/{modelId}/artifacts/{artifactId}/compose). type app needs app: name and version (0 takes the latest) from GET /apps. Both take env, written to a .env file next to the deployed files; names match [A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*, values hold no line break and no single quote.

Each target is {kind: node, nsId, infraId, nodeId, sshUser}. The cloud, region, zone, address, SSH user and SSH key are read from the node in CB-Tumblebug (public IP, or private IP when there is none). sshUser is optional (1 to 32 characters matching [a-z_][a-z0-9_-]*) and replaces the SSH user CB-Tumblebug reports (nodeUserName) in the Semaphore inventory, while the key stays the one CB-Tumblebug holds. Without sshUser, before the playbooks of a node run, the service logs in to the node over SSH with that key (authentication only, no command, 10 seconds per attempt, at most 6 attempts) as the CB-Tumblebug user and keeps it when the node accepts it. CB-Tumblebug creates its login user cb-user with useradd -G sudo, which fails on images without a sudo group (RHEL, Rocky, AlmaLinux and Amazon Linux use wheel), and such a node has no cb-user, while the image default user accepts the same key. So when the node refuses the CB-Tumblebug user, the default users of the node image (from its osType: ec2-user for Amazon Linux, RHEL and SUSE, rocky, almalinux then ec2-user, centos, fedora, opc then ec2-user for Oracle Linux, admin for Debian, ubuntu; ec2-user, ubuntu and admin for an OS not recognized; never root) are tried in order and the first accepted is used, with a note naming both users. When every user is refused, or the node cannot be reached yet (still booting), the CB-Tumblebug user is kept and a note says so; install-docker then waits for the node as before. nodes[].sshUser and nodes[].steps[].sshUser record the user the playbooks ran as, and nodes[].sshUserSource where it came from (request, tumblebug or fallback). kind k8s is reserved and answered with 422. When gpu is omitted it is taken from the node spec (acceleratorType gpu); a spec that cannot be read means no GPU, and nodes[].notes says why.

For every node, in parallel up to a bound: the files are placed in <AIAPP_STAGE_ROOT>/<id>/<csp>-<nodeId>/, then Semaphore runs install-docker (with the NVIDIA Container Toolkit on a GPU node) and then compose-up (inference, which waits for the runtime health path from the node itself and, when the node uses the GPU, checks that the runtime runs on it: a vllm process in nvidia-smi, or an ollama log line of inference compute on CUDA or ROCm; the line found is kept in nodes[].gpuCheck) or copy-and-run (app, which runs the app script from the folder the files are copied to, then waits until every app port answers HTTP and fails the node when a container of the project restarted or exited with a non-zero code). On the node the files go to /opt/aiapp/<work key> and run as compose project aiapp-<work key>, where the work key is ms-<runtimeId> for an inference service and app-<name> for an app; nodes[].workKey and nodes[].nodeDir record them. Deploying the same work key to a node again replaces the previous deployment there. The SSH key is registered in Semaphore for the run only and deleted afterwards; it is never part of a record, a log or a response.

Once the playbooks of a node succeed, the ports the deployment serves (nodes[].ports: the runtime port of an inference service; for an app, app.ports or else the ports the app version was uploaded with) are opened over TCP inbound from 0.0.0.0/0 in every CB-Tumblebug security group the node lists (securityGroupIds). Ports a group already lets in are not sent again. nodes[].openedPorts lists, per group and port, whether the rule was added or already there. A port that cannot be opened does not fail the node: nodes[].portsError says why and a note points to it. AIAPP_DEPLOYMENT_OPEN_PORTS=false (true by default) turns port opening off; the ports are then only recorded, with a note. A dry run opens nothing; nodes[].ports still lists the ports it would open.

The request is checked against the catalogs first: a malformed request is 400, an unknown model, artifact, runtime or app is 404, and an artifact the runtime cannot run is 422. Every target node is then read from CB-Tumblebug: a node or infra CB-Tumblebug does not have is 404 naming the target nsId/infraId/nodeId, and CB-Tumblebug failing or not answering is 502. A refused request leaves no record. An accepted request answers 202 with the record in status pending; follow it with GET /deployments/{id}/progress until done is true (or GET /deployments/{id} for the whole record). With dry run on (AIAPP_TUMBLEBUG_DRY_RUN), only the node look-up and the file placement are done, nothing is registered in Semaphore, and the finished record (status dry-run, with the rendered compose and the node addresses) is returned with 200.

delete.description:
Stop and remove the containers of a deployment on every node: Semaphore runs compose-down, which is docker compose -p aiapp-<work key> down --remove-orphans, as the SSH user the node was deployed as (nodes[].sshUser, which is targets[].sshUser when the request gave it, or the image default user the deployment fell back to); no SSH login is tried again. Named volumes (for example model weights a runtime downloaded) and the node folder /opt/aiapp/<work key> are kept, so that the next deployment of the work key finds them. A node without the project has nothing to take down and succeeds. The ports the deployment opened (nodes[].openedPorts) stay open in the CB-Tumblebug security groups, since other workloads may share them; close them in CB-Tumblebug when needed.

Only the latest deployment of a work key on a node is live there. A node where a later deployment of the same work key replaced this one is not touched, since stopping the project would stop the later deployment; it is marked removed and nodes[].notes names the later deployment. A node of a dry-run deployment, a node where the deployment never started its service (compose-up or copy-and-run never ran), and a node CB-Tumblebug no longer has are marked removed without running anything, each with a note.

When some node needs compose-down, the answer is 202 with the record in status removing and nodes[].status removing; follow it with GET /deployments/{id} until it is removed (every node) or remove-failed (compose-down failed on some node; nodes[].error says why). DELETE again retries the nodes not removed yet. When no node needs compose-down, the finished record (status removed) is returned with 200. A deployment already removed is returned as it is with 200. With dry run on (AIAPP_TUMBLEBUG_DRY_RUN), nothing is sent to Semaphore: nodes that would be taken down keep their status and get a note, and the record is returned with 200. Every removal is archived (kind node-removal).

Every call is archived (kind node-control).

get.description:
Read the short progress of a deployment of either type (inference or app), made to be polled every few seconds after POST /deployments answers 202, and after DELETE /deployments/{id} answers 202, until done is true. It is computed from the deployment record and asks no node and no other service.

done is false while the deployment is pending, deploying or removing, and true otherwise. running is true only when it ended running (the service is up on every node). A finished deployment that is not running is failed, partial (count.running and count.failed tell how many nodes), interrupted (the service restarted while it ran), dry-run, or removed or remove-failed once taken down. count has total, inProgress (pending, deploying, removing), running, failed (failed, interrupted, remove-failed), dryRun and removed.

For every node: status, done, phase (reading-node, staging, checking-ssh, waiting-node-lock, install-docker, compose-up, copy-and-run, compose-down, opening-ports, done; a failed node keeps the phase it failed in) with phaseStartedAt, the last playbook started (step: playbook, Semaphore taskId and taskUrl as soon as the task starts, its status waiting, starting or running while it runs and success, error, stopped or rejected once it ended, and currentTask, the Ansible task it is on, such as "Wait until the service answers"), stepsDone of stepsTotal, error, host, serviceUrl and ports. The task status and currentTask are read from Semaphore every 5 seconds while the playbook runs.

get.description:
List the addresses of what serves on the nodes now, derived from the deployment records of POST /deployments: one endpoint per node and work key (ms-<runtimeId> for an inference service, app-<name> for an app). Each filter is optional and matched exactly; all given filters must match. Endpoints are ordered by nsId, infraId, nodeId and workKey.

On a node, a work key is decided by the latest deployment of it there (by creation time) that is pending or deploying, that started its service (compose-up or copy-and-run ran), or that was taken down after starting it. It has an endpoint only when that deployment is running on the node. So a redeploy replaces the endpoint with the new deploymentId; DELETE /deployments/{id} removes it, and an older deployment of the same work key does not come back, since compose-down stopped the project they share; a later deployment that failed after it started its service leaves no endpoint, since the shared project was recreated and the older containers are gone; a later deployment that failed before that (for example in install-docker) leaves the older endpoint as it was; one still pending or deploying leaves none until it ends. Dry-run deployments never make an endpoint.

Every node with an endpoint is read from CB-Tumblebug on each call, once per node. nodeStatus is the node status CB-Tumblebug gives (Running, Suspended, Terminated, Failed, ...), unknown when CB-Tumblebug could not be read, or not-found when it no longer has the node; the endpoint is listed in every case. available is true only when the node is Running; only then are host and the URLs set, built from the current public IP of the node, or its private IP when it has none. A node that is not Running has no address, since its IP may change when it is resumed.

An inference endpoint carries runtimeId, modelId, artifactId, url (the OpenAI compatible API, http://<host>:<port><apiBasePath>) and healthUrl. An app endpoint carries name, version and urls, one http://<host>:<port> per port it serves. portsOpened is true when every served port was found or added in a CB-Tumblebug security group of the node; otherwise the URLs may not be reachable from outside, and portsError or notes say why.

post.description:
Run one fixed workflow as ordered AI-App tool calls, without a model, and archive the run.
deploy takes the node deployment request of POST /deployments (model.NodeDeploymentReq: {type, targets, inference | app}); it reads the model (get_model) or the application (get_app), creates the deployment (create_deployment) and reads it (get_deployment) until every node ended. An inference service is checked to answer by the compose-up playbook inside the deployment. A deployment that succeeded on some nodes only (partial) fails the run.
heal takes {deploymentId}; a deployment that is failed, partial, interrupted or a dry run is created once more from the request it was made with, and followed the same way. A deployment running on every node is left alone, a pending or deploying one is refused.
control takes {deploymentId, action} with action suspend, resume, reboot or terminate (control_node).
status takes {deploymentId} and reports the deployment record and the last task output lines of every node (get_deployment, get_deployment_logs).
A step held by the AI-App dry-run gate is reported as blocked and the steps that need it as waiting. A run whose steps failed is still returned with 200 and status failed. Served by the automation engine and forwarded by the AI-App service

get.description:
Check, at the time of the call, what deploying onto nodes depends on, and answer 200 with what was found whether or not each dependency is up. Nothing is created or changed in any of them.

semaphore: whether GET /api/ping answers (reachable, latencyMs), whether the configured token or user name and password are accepted (authenticated), the version from /api/info, whether the project (AIAPP_SEMAPHORE_PROJECT) exists and whether the template of each deployment playbook (aiapp-install-docker, aiapp-compose-up, aiapp-copy-and-run, aiapp-compose-down) exists. A project or template that does not exist yet is not a fault: the first deployment that needs it creates it. uiUrl is AIAPP_SEMAPHORE_UI_URL, the web UI that the taskUrl of each recorded playbook run points at; without it records carry no task links. tumblebug: whether CB-Tumblebug GET /readyz answers. stage: whether a file can be created in AIAPP_STAGE_ROOT. dryRun and openPorts are AIAPP_TUMBLEBUG_DRY_RUN and AIAPP_DEPLOYMENT_OPEN_PORTS. Each check gives up after 5 seconds. URLs are shown without credentials and no credential is part of the response.

GET /readyz stays the liveness probe: it says only whether this service started, and calls nothing.
List every tool the agent may call, with its risk grade and whether the dry-run guard applies. Exposed so another agent framework can adopt the same tool surface
Serve the single page console that calls this service's own API

counts.description:
Counts is what the returned models did to the catalog. All zero when
the source was skipped or its fetch failed: the catalog is not touched
then.

error.description:
Error is why the last fetch from the source failed. Empty when it did
not.

fetched.description: Fetched is how many models the source returned.

name.description: Name is the source, the origin its models are stored with.

reachable.description:
Reachable is whether the source's host answered the check before the
last run, and CheckedAt is when that check was made. Both are absent
until the source has been checked once.

skipped.description:
Skipped is why the last run did not fetch from the source:
"unreachable" when its host did not answer. The catalog is not touched
then. Empty when the source was fetched.

startedAt.description:
StartedAt and FinishedAt bound the last run of the source. Both are
absent until the source has run once.

unreachable.description:
Unreachable is why the reachability check failed, such as a timeout
or a TLS certificate the client does not trust. Empty when the host
answered.

enabled.description: Enabled is false when AIAPP_CATALOG_SYNC_ENABLED is off.

interval.description:
Interval is how long the sync waits between scheduled runs while a
source is reachable, as a Go duration. Empty when the sync is disabled.

nextRunAt.description:
NextRunAt is when the next scheduled run starts. Absent while a run is
in progress, before the schedule has started and when the sync is
disabled.

offline.description:
Offline is true when the last run reached no source. The schedule then
retries sooner than the interval: after 5m, 15m, then every 1h, never
later than the interval.

removed.description:
Removed counts, by origin, the entries the last run deleted because
their origin is a sync source that is not configured
(AIAPP_CATALOG_SYNC_SOURCES). Entries of origin seed or manual are
never deleted. Absent when the last run deleted none.

running.description: Running is true while a run is in progress.

sources.description:
Sources holds the last result of each configured source, in the
configured order.

dryRun.description: DryRun is the AI-App dry-run state, as of the current MCP session.

registration.description:
Registration is how the last registry registration went. It is left out
of the card sent to the registry.

usesLLM.description: UsesLLM is always false: the workflows are fixed.

uses.description:
Uses names the AI-App tools the engine calls, whether or not it is
connected. A tool carries its grade only while the engine is connected
to an AI-App service that publishes it.

dryRun.description: DryRun is the AI-App dry-run state the run executed under.

limit.description: Limit is the most items one response holds.

offset.description: Offset is how many items of the list come before the first one returned.

total.description: Total is how many items the filters keep, before the page is cut.

message.description:
Message says why a step was blocked, waits or was skipped, or what its
result meant for the workflow.

output.description: Output is the tool result as the AI-App service returned it.

startedAt.description: StartedAt and EndedAt are absent on a step that was not run.

tool.description: Tool is the AI-App MCP tool the step calls.

unconfirmed.description: Unconfirmed means the create response was lost or unreadable.

grade.description: Grade is one of read, review, write, destructive.

status.description: Status is disabled, pending, registered or failed.

name.description:
Name identifies the application: lower case letters, digits, "_" and
"-", at most 63 characters. Uploading again under the same name adds a
version.

versions.description: Versions are the uploaded versions, oldest first.

name.description:
Name is the file name on the node: letters, digits, ".", "_", "+" and
"-", not starting with ".", at most 255 characters.

sha256.description: SHA256 is the hex encoded SHA-256 digest of the file content.

sizeBytes.description: SizeBytes is the file size in bytes.

limit.description: Limit is the most items one response holds.

offset.description: Offset is how many items of the list come before the first one returned.

total.description: Total is how many items the filters keep, before the page is cut.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt is when the version was registered.

files.description:
Files are the uploaded files, in upload order. They are copied flat into
the folder the script runs in.

ports.description:
Ports are the TCP ports the application serves on the node. A
deployment opens them inbound in the node's CB-Tumblebug security
groups. Empty opens nothing.

script.description:
Script is the shell script run on the node from the folder the files
are copied to. At most 64 KiB.

version.description:
Version numbers the uploads of one name from 1, one higher than the
highest version present when it was uploaded.

limit.description: Limit is the most items one response holds.

offset.description: Offset is how many items of the list come before the first one returned.

total.description: Total is how many items the filters keep, before the page is cut.

deployable.description:
Deployable is true when runtimes lists at least one runtime. It is
computed and ignored on input.

format.description:
Format is the file format the runtime loads: hf for Hugging Face
safetensors, gguf for GGUF. Filter with ?format=.

id.description:
ID identifies the artifact within its model, with the same character
rules as a model ID.

parameters.description:
Parameters is the parameter count of this artifact as the source
writes it, such as 8.2B or 751.63M. Empty means unknown.

precision.description:
Precision is the precision or quantization exactly as the source states
it, such as BF16, FP8 or Q4_K_M. It is not normalized. Empty means
unknown.

ref.description:
Ref is the name of the artifact at its source: a Hugging Face repository
id, an Ollama model tag, or an image reference.

runtimes.description:
Runtimes are the inference runtimes known to load this artifact. Each
runtime must be listed explicitly: the same file format may load in one
runtime version and not in another. Filter with ?runtimeId=. An empty
list means no runtime is known to load the artifact: it is listed but
cannot be deployed.

sizeGiB.description:
SizeGiB is the download size in GiB (2^30 bytes). Zero or absent means
unknown.

source.description:
Source is where the artifact is downloaded from, such as huggingface,
kaggle, ollama or docker-model-runner. Filter with ?source=.

latencyMs.description:
LatencyMs is how long the reachability call took, in milliseconds.
Absent when it did not answer.

message.description: Message says what was found, or why a check failed.

url.description: URL is where it is called, without credentials.

version.description: Version is the version it reports, when it reports one.

apiKey.description:
APIKey is what callers of url send as `Authorization: Bearer
<apiKey>`. Inference only, for runtimes that take a key (vllm), and
set whether or not the endpoint is available: the key does not change
with the address.

artifactId.description: ArtifactID is the artifact of that model. Inference only.

available.description:
Available is true when the node is Running and has an address; only
then are host and the URLs set.

csp.description: CSP is the cloud of the node, in lower case.

deployedAt.description: DeployedAt is when the deployment finished on the node.

deploymentId.description:
DeploymentID is the deployment serving the work key on the node; read
it with GET /deployments/{id} and take it down with
DELETE /deployments/{id}.

healthUrl.description:
HealthURL answers 200 once the runtime is up:
http://<host>:<runtime port><runtime healthPath>. Inference only, and
only when available and the runtime profile names a health path.

host.description:
Host is the address the URLs are built from: the current public IP of
the node, or its private IP when it has none. Absent when not
available.

infraId.description: InfraID is the CB-Tumblebug Infra of the node.

modelId.description: ModelID is the model of the model catalog served. Inference only.

name.description: Name is the uploaded application. App only.

nodeId.description: NodeID is the node within the Infra.

nodeStatus.description:
NodeStatus is the node status CB-Tumblebug gives when the endpoints are
listed, such as Running, Suspended, Terminated or Failed; unknown when
CB-Tumblebug could not be read, not-found when it no longer has the
node.

notes.description:
Notes are the notes of the node result, such as port opening being
turned off.

nsId.description: NsID is the CB-Tumblebug namespace of the node.

openedPorts.description:
OpenedPorts are, per security group and port, the inbound rules found
or added when the deployment ran.

ports.description: Ports are the TCP ports the deployment serves on the node.

portsError.description: PortsError is why some ports could not be opened.

portsOpened.description:
PortsOpened is true when every port in ports was found or added as an
inbound rule in a CB-Tumblebug security group of the node and no port
failed. False means the URLs may not be reachable from outside the
node: portsError or notes say why.

region.description: Region and Zone are where the node runs.

runtimeId.description: RuntimeID is the inference runtime profile. Inference only.

url.description:
URL is the OpenAI compatible API of an inference service:
http://<host>:<runtime port><runtime apiBasePath>. Inference only, and
only when available.

urls.description:
URLs are http://<host>:<port> for every port the application serves.
App only; absent when not available or the application serves no port.

version.description: Version is the application version deployed. App only.

workKey.description:
WorkKey is what serves on the node: ms-<runtimeId> for an inference
service, app-<name> for an application. A node serves one endpoint per
work key.

endpoints.description: Endpoints are ordered by nsId, infraId, nodeId and workKey.

limit.description: Limit is the most items one response holds.

offset.description: Offset is how many items of the list come before the first one returned.

total.description: Total is how many items the filters keep, before the page is cut.

artifacts.description:
Artifacts are the published forms of the model that a runtime can load.
At least one is required.

contextLength.description:
ContextLength is the context window in tokens. Zero or absent means
unknown, not unlimited.

deployable.description:
Deployable is true when some artifact is deployable. It is computed
from the artifacts and ignored on input. Filter with ?deployable=.

description.description:
Description is what the source says the model is, copied as written.
Empty when the source gives none.
description.example: Qwen3-VL is the vision-language model of the Qwen3 series.

family.description: Family is the model family the model belongs to.

id.description:
ID is the catalog identifier: lower case letters, digits, ".", "_" and
"-", at most 63 characters.

inputModalities.description:
InputModalities are the kinds of input the model accepts, such as text or
image. Filter with ?modality=.

license.description: License is the license identifier of the weights. Empty means unknown.

name.description: Name is the display name, usually the name the publisher uses.

origin.description:
Origin is who put the model in the catalog: seed for a built-in model,
manual for a model registered or edited through POST /models, or the
source the catalog sync collected it from (huggingface, ollama,
docker-model-runner, ngc, kaggle). Absent is read as manual. POST /models
always records manual. Filter with ?origin=.

parameters.description:
Parameters is the parameter count as the publisher writes it. A model
whose artifacts differ in size, such as the size tags of an Ollama
model, leaves it empty and states it on each artifact.

publisher.description: Publisher is who released the model.

stale.description:
Stale is true when the source of a collected model no longer lists it.
The entry is kept, and turns false again when the source lists it again.

syncedAt.description:
SyncedAt is the last time the catalog sync saw the model at its source.
Absent for a model the sync does not keep.

tasks.description:
Tasks are what the model is used for, such as chat, vision-chat or
embedding. Filter with ?task=.

limit.description: Limit is the most items one response holds.

offset.description: Offset is how many items of the list come before the first one returned.

total.description: Total is how many items the filters keep, before the page is cut.

env.description:
Env is written to the .env file in the folder the script runs in, and
exported before the script starts. Names match [A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*; values
hold no line break and no single quote. Addresses of other nodes go
here.

envFrom.description: EnvFrom maps application variables to AIAPP_DEPLOY_SECRET_* on the AI-App server.

inferenceBinding.description: InferenceBinding resolves connection values from a running deployment on the same node.

ports.description:
Ports replace, for this deployment, the ports the application version
was uploaded with: the TCP ports opened inbound in the node's
CB-Tumblebug security groups, each from 1 to 65535, at most 16.
Omitted takes the version's ports.

version.description:
Version is the version to deploy. 0 takes the latest; the record keeps
the version taken.

action.description: Action is passed to CB-Tumblebug node control.

nodes.description: Nodes are the per node results, in deployment order.

message.description: Message is the CB-Tumblebug answer, or why nothing was sent.

status.description:
Status is done, failed, or blocked when nothing was sent because the
service or the deployment is in dry run.

csp.description: CSP is the cloud, from connectionConfig.providerName, in lower case.

host.description: Host is the public IP, or the private IP when the node has none.

region.description: Region and Zone are where the node runs.

specId.description: SpecID is the node spec in CB-Tumblebug.

user.description:
User is the SSH user CB-Tumblebug reports for the node. The
playbooks ran as nodes[].sshUser, which differs when the target
gave sshUser or the node refused this user (sshUserSource).

apiKey.description:
APIKey is the key the vllm service on the node takes as
`Authorization: Bearer <apiKey>`: the one the request gave, or the one
this node kept from its previous deployment of the work key, or a new
random one. It is kept in plain text in the deployment store, as env
values are. Absent for runtimes without a key.

compose.description: Compose is the rendered docker-compose.yml of an inference service.

error.description: Error is why the node failed, or why taking it down failed.

finishedAt.description: FinishedAt is when work on the node ended.

gpu.description:
GPU is whether the runtime was given the node's GPUs and the NVIDIA
Container Toolkit was installed.

gpuCheck.description:
GPUCheck is, for an inference service given the GPU, what compose-up
found on the node showing that the runtime runs on it: the method
(nvidia-smi or log) and the nvidia-smi compute process or the log line.
When the runtime is not on the GPU the node fails instead. Absent
without GPU, for an app and for a dry run.

gpuSource.description:
GPUSource says where GPU came from: request, spec, or default when the
spec could not be read.

node.description:
Node is how the node was reached, as read from CB-Tumblebug. Absent
when the node could not be read. The SSH key is never included.

nodeDir.description:
NodeDir is the folder on the node the files were copied to,
/opt/aiapp/<work key>. Its compose project is aiapp-<work key>.

notes.description:
Notes record decisions made for this node, such as why the spec could
not be read.

openedPorts.description:
OpenedPorts are, per security group and port, the inbound rules found
or added in CB-Tumblebug. Taking the deployment down closes none of
them, since other workloads may share the group.

phase.description:
Phase is what the service is doing on the node: reading-node (the node
and its SSH key are read from CB-Tumblebug), staging (the files are
placed in the stage folder), checking-ssh (the SSH user is tried),
waiting-node-lock (another deployment of the same work key on the node
runs first), install-docker, compose-up, copy-and-run or compose-down
(that playbook runs; steps[] holds its task), opening-ports (the served
ports are opened in the security groups) and done once the node
succeeded. A node that failed keeps the phase it failed in. Absent until
work on the node begins, and for records written before phases were
kept.

phaseStartedAt.description: PhaseStartedAt is when the node entered Phase.

ports.description:
Ports are the TCP ports the deployment serves on the node: the runtime
port of an inference service, the ports of an application. They are
opened inbound from 0.0.0.0/0 in every security group of the node once
the playbooks succeed. A dry run and a failed node open none; with
port opening turned off (AIAPP_DEPLOYMENT_OPEN_PORTS=false) none are
opened and notes says so.

portsError.description:
PortsError is why some ports could not be opened. The node still
succeeds; the ports can be opened in CB-Tumblebug by hand.

removedAt.description: RemovedAt is when the deployment was taken down from the node.

serviceUrl.description:
ServiceURL is the inference API on the node, built from the public or
private IP the node was reached at, the runtime port and its API base
path. Inference services only.

sshUser.description:
SSHUser is the SSH user the playbooks ran as on the node: the
target's sshUser when given. Otherwise node.user, the one CB-Tumblebug
reports, is tried with the node key before the playbooks run; when the
node refuses it, the default users of the node image (such as ec2-user
on RHEL and Amazon Linux) are tried and the first it accepts is taken.
Taking the deployment down runs as the same user.

sshUserSource.description:
SSHUserSource says where SSHUser came from: request (targets[].sshUser),
tumblebug (node.user, which the node accepted, or which was kept because
the login could not be tried or every user was refused; notes say which)
or fallback (an image default user, taken after the node refused
node.user; notes name both).

stageDir.description:
StageDir is the folder the files were placed in on the shared stage
volume: <AIAPP_STAGE_ROOT>/<deployment id>/<csp>-<node id>.

startedAt.description: StartedAt is when work on the node began.

status.description:
Status is pending, deploying, running, failed, dry-run or interrupted;
once taken down, removing, removed or remove-failed.

steps.description:
Steps are the playbooks run on the node, in order. A step that failed
ends the node.

target.description: Target is the target as requested.

workKey.description:
WorkKey names what the deployment occupies on the node: ms-<runtime>
for an inference service, app-<name> for an application. A later deployment of
the same work key to the same node replaces this one there.

cleanupErrors.description:
CleanupErrors name the Semaphore key or inventory of this run that
could not be deleted. A key named here may still be stored in Semaphore.

currentTask.description:
CurrentTask is the Ansible task the playbook is on, from the last
TASK [...] line of the log so far, such as "Wait until the service
answers". Once the playbook ended it is the task it stopped on when it
did not succeed, and empty when it succeeded.

error.description: Error is why the run could not be registered, started or followed.

output.description:
Output is the task log, one line per entry: the log so far while the
task runs, then the whole log. It is returned by
GET /deployments/{id}/logs and left out of the deployment record.

playbook.description:
Playbook is install-docker.yml, compose-up.yml, copy-and-run.yml, or
compose-down.yml when the deployment was taken down.

sshUser.description: SSHUser is the SSH user the playbook ran as.

status.description:
Status is the Semaphore task status: waiting, starting, running or
stopping while the task runs (read every 5 seconds), then the final one,
success, error, stopped or rejected. Empty while the task is being
registered and when it never started. TaskID and TaskURL are set as soon
as the task starts.

taskId.description: TaskID is the Semaphore task, kept in Semaphore with its log.

taskUrl.description:
TaskURL is the page of the task in the Semaphore web UI, with its log.
Absent when the task never started or AIAPP_SEMAPHORE_UI_URL was not
set when it ran.

infraId.description: InfraID is the CB-Tumblebug Infra the node belongs to.

kind.description:
Kind is "node". "k8s" is reserved for Kubernetes clusters and refused
with 422.

nodeId.description: NodeID is the node within the Infra.

nsId.description: NsID is the CB-Tumblebug namespace of the Infra.

sshUser.description:
SSHUser replaces, for this node, the SSH user CB-Tumblebug reports
(nodeUserName) in the Semaphore inventory; the SSH key is still the one
CB-Tumblebug holds for the node. Without it, the CB-Tumblebug user is
tried with the key before the playbooks run, and when the node refuses
it (CB-Tumblebug could not create cb-user on the image), the image's
default users are tried. Give it to choose the user, and no login is
tried. 1 to 32 characters matching [a-z_][a-z0-9_-]*. Taking the
deployment down uses the user recorded at deploy time.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt is when the request was accepted.

dryRun.description:
DryRun is true when the service ran with dry run on: only the node
look-up and file placement were done.

error.description: Error is why the deployment as a whole stopped, when it did.

finishedAt.description: FinishedAt is when the last node finished. Absent while it runs.

id.description:
ID is a UUID (version 4). It names the stage folder. The folder on each
node is named after the work key instead; see NodeDeployResult.NodeDir.

nodes.description: Nodes are the per node results, in request order.

removedAt.description:
RemovedAt is when taking the deployment down ended, removed or
remove-failed. Absent until then.

request.description:
Request is the request as accepted, with the runtime and app version
that were taken filled in.

status.description:
Status is pending, deploying, running (every node), failed (every
node), partial (some nodes), dry-run (files placed, nothing run) or
interrupted (the service stopped while it was deploying); once taken
down with DELETE /deployments/{id}, removing, removed or remove-failed.

deployments.description: Deployments are ordered newest first, without task output.

limit.description: Limit is the most items one response holds.

offset.description: Offset is how many items of the list come before the first one returned.

total.description: Total is how many items the filters keep, before the page is cut.

nodes.description: Nodes hold, per target, the steps with their output.

count.description: Count is how many nodes are in each state.

done.description:
Done is false while the service still works on the deployment
(pending, deploying or removing) and true otherwise: polling can stop.

elapsedSeconds.description:
ElapsedSeconds runs from createdAt to finishedAt (or removedAt once
taken down), or to now while the deployment is not done.

error.description: Error is why the deployment as a whole stopped, when it did.

finishedAt.description:
FinishedAt is when the last node finished deploying; RemovedAt when
taking it down ended.

nodes.description: Nodes are the per node progress, in request order.

running.description:
Running is true when the deployment ended with its service up on every
node (status running). A dry run, and a deployment taken down, is Done
without Running.

status.description: Status is the deployment status, as in GET /deployments/{id}.

app.description: App is required when type is app.

inference.description: Inference is required when type is inference.

requireDryRun.description: RequireDryRun rejects the request if the receiving AI-App could run playbooks.

targets.description: Targets are the nodes to deploy to, at most 32, each once.

type.description:
Type is "inference" or "app"; the field of the same name below carries
what to deploy.

previousDeploymentId.description: PreviousDeploymentID is the last accepted deployment for this work key, or empty for a free placement.

native.description: Native requests Ollama's native URL. The default is the OpenAI-compatible URL.

apiKey.description:
APIKey is the key callers of a vllm service send as
`Authorization: Bearer <apiKey>` on /v1 paths; /health stays open. It
is 16 to 128 characters of [A-Za-z0-9._~-]. Omitted, each node keeps
the key of its previous deployment of the same work key, or gets a
new random one. The key is given to vLLM as the VLLM_API_KEY
environment variable and shown in the node results and on
GET /endpoints. Runtime ollama has no key and refuses one.

args.description:
Args are appended to the runtime command after the arguments this
service sets and the catalog arguments of the artifact
(runtimes[].args). For vllm they follow `vllm serve --model <ref>
--port <port>` (and --runner pooling for an embedding model) and the
catalog arguments, for example ["--max-model-len", "32768"]; vllm takes
the last value of a repeated flag, so they override the catalog
arguments. At most 32, each 1 to 256 characters
without control characters; --model, --port and --host are set by the
service and refused. Runtime ollama takes none and refuses them.

artifactId.description: ArtifactID is an artifact of that model.

gpu.description:
GPU reserves every NVIDIA GPU of the node for the runtime and installs
the NVIDIA Container Toolkit. Omitted, it is true when the node spec in
CB-Tumblebug has acceleratorType gpu, and false when the spec cannot be
read; the node result says which.

modelId.description: ModelID is a model of the model catalog (GET /models).

runtimeId.description:
RuntimeID is a runtime profile ID (GET /runtimes) the artifact lists.
Empty takes the first runtime the artifact lists.

result.description:
Result is added when this deployment added the rule, existing when an
inbound rule of the group already opened the port to 0.0.0.0/0.

securityGroupId.description:
SecurityGroupID is the CB-Tumblebug security group, in the namespace
of the target.

done.description: Done is true once the node is no longer pending, deploying or removing.

error.description: Error is why the node failed.

host.description: Host is the address the node was reached at (nodes[].node.host).

phase.description:
Phase is nodes[].phase of the record: where the node is, or where it
failed.

ports.description: Ports are the TCP ports the deployment serves on the node.

serviceUrl.description: ServiceURL is the inference API on the node (inference only).

status.description: Status is the node status, as in GET /deployments/{id}.

step.description: Step is the last playbook started on the node, without its log.

stepsDone.description:
StepsDone counts the playbooks of StepsTotal that succeeded. StepsTotal
is 2 for a deployment (install-docker, then compose-up or
copy-and-run), 1 while or after taking it down (compose-down), and 0
for a dry run.

failed.description: Failed are failed, interrupted or remove-failed.

inProgress.description: InProgress are pending, deploying or removing.

args.description:
Args are arguments the runtime needs for this artifact, such as a
context length that fits the GPU memory. They are appended after the
arguments the service sets and before the inference.args of a deploy
request; vLLM takes the last value when a flag repeats, so the request
can override them. Only vllm takes them.

minVersion.description:
MinVersion is the oldest runtime version known to load the artifact.
Empty means not recorded.

runtimeId.description: RuntimeID is the runtime profile ID, as listed by GET /runtimes.

verifiedAt.description:
VerifiedAt is when an inference deployment of this artifact on this
runtime last succeeded on a node. A dry run does not count. Absent means
never verified. Filter with ?verified=.

apiBasePath.description:
APIBasePath is the path of the OpenAI compatible API, appended to
http://<node>:<port> by whoever calls the inference service.

formats.description: Formats are the artifact formats this runtime loads.

healthPath.description: HealthPath answers 200 once the runtime is up.

id.description: ID is the runtime identifier artifacts refer to in runtimes[].runtimeId.

image.description: Image is the container image, pinned to a release tag.

port.description:
Port is the TCP port the runtime serves its API on, inside the container
and on the node.

authenticated.description:
Authenticated is whether the configured token, or user name and
password, were accepted.

configured.description: Configured is false when AIAPP_SEMAPHORE_URL is not set.

latencyMs.description:
LatencyMs is how long the reachability call took, in milliseconds.
Absent when it did not answer.

message.description: Message says what was found, or why a check failed.

project.description:
Project is the Semaphore project deployments are registered in
(AIAPP_SEMAPHORE_PROJECT).

projectId.description:
ProjectID is the project's ID. Absent when it does not exist yet or
could not be read.

templates.description:
Templates are the templates of the deployment playbooks, each with
whether it exists. Every one reads as missing when the project could
not be read.

uiUrl.description:
UIURL is the web UI the task links of deployment records point at
(AIAPP_SEMAPHORE_UI_URL). Absent when it is not set, and then the
records carry no task links.

url.description: URL is where it is called, without credentials.

version.description: Version is the version it reports, when it reports one.

exists.description: Exists is false until the first deployment that runs the playbook.

id.description: ID is the template's ID. Absent when it does not exist.

checkedAt.description: CheckedAt is when the checks ran.

dryRun.description:
DryRun is true when deployments stop after placing their files and
node control is blocked (AIAPP_TUMBLEBUG_DRY_RUN). Semaphore is not
called then.

openPorts.description:
OpenPorts is true when a deployment opens the ports it serves in the
node's CB-Tumblebug security groups (AIAPP_DEPLOYMENT_OPEN_PORTS).

stage.description: Stage is the folder deployment files are placed in for Semaphore.

tumblebug.description: Tumblebug is the CB-Tumblebug the nodes are read from.

writable.description: Writable is whether a file could be created in it.

grade.description: Grade is one of read, review, write, destructive.

guardedByDryRun.description: GuardedByDryRun is true when the dry-run setting can block this tool.

executed.description: Executed is false when the dry-run guard blocked an infrastructure change.

grade.description: Grade is the tool risk grade that decided whether the call was executed.

added.description: Added is how many fetched models were new to the catalog.

invalid.description:
Invalid is how many fetched models were dropped because they do not
validate or repeat an ID earlier in the same fetch.

skipped.description:
Skipped is how many fetched models were left alone because the catalog
holds an entry of the same ID from another origin.

staled.description:
Staled is how many entries of the origin the fetch did not return. Each
is marked stale, whether or not it already was.

updated.description: Updated is how many entries of the origin were replaced from the fetch.

reason.description: Reason says, for a person, why the candidate was picked.
reason.example: Chat interface that talks to an OpenAI compatible API

score.description:
Score ranks the candidate: higher is better. The scale is the
recommender's own.

version.description: Version is a version of that application.

gpuCount.description:
GPUCount is the number of GPUs available on one node. 0 means no GPU;
absent means unknown. At most 64.

gpuMemoryGiB.description: GPUMemoryGiB is the memory of one GPU in GiB (2^30 bytes).

inference.description:
Inference are the inference services the application is to use, each
naming a model of the catalog.

maxCandidates.description:
MaxCandidates bounds the candidates returned, at most 50. 0 leaves it to
the recommender.

maxSizeGiB.description:
MaxSizeGiB is the largest download, in GiB, the caller accepts for one
model artifact or application.

requirements.description:
Requirements carry anything else the recommender reads. The keys are the
recommender's own; the service passes them through unread.

targetNodes.description: TargetNodes are the nodes the application is meant to run on, at most 32.

tasks.description:
Tasks are what the application is to be used for, such as chat-ui, rag
or travel-planner. Uploaded applications carry no tags, so the words are
the recommender's own.

candidates.description:
Candidates are ordered best first. Empty means no uploaded application
fits.

recommender.description:
Recommender is the name of the implementation that answered, as set in
AIAPP_RECOMMENDER_APP.

artifactId.description: ArtifactID is an artifact of that model. Empty means any.

modelId.description: ModelID is a model of the model catalog (GET /models).

runtimeId.description: RuntimeID is the runtime profile that serves it. Empty means any.

artifactId.description: ArtifactID is an artifact of that model.

modelId.description: ModelID is a model of the model catalog (GET /models).

reason.description: Reason says, for a person, why the candidate was picked.
reason.example: Accepts text and image input and fits one 24 GiB GPU in BF16

runtimeId.description: RuntimeID is a runtime profile the artifact lists.

score.description:
Score ranks the candidate: higher is better. The scale is the
recommender's own.

gpuCount.description:
GPUCount is the number of GPUs available on one node. 0 means no GPU;
absent means unknown. At most 64.

gpuMemoryGiB.description: GPUMemoryGiB is the memory of one GPU in GiB (2^30 bytes).

inputModalities.description:
InputModalities are the kinds of input the model must accept, in the
words of the catalog inputModalities[]: text or image.

maxCandidates.description:
MaxCandidates bounds the candidates returned, at most 50. 0 leaves it to
the recommender.

maxSizeGiB.description:
MaxSizeGiB is the largest download, in GiB, the caller accepts for one
model artifact or application.

requirements.description:
Requirements carry anything else the recommender reads, such as a cost
budget, a latency target or a language. The keys are the recommender's
own; the service passes them through unread.

runtimeId.description:
RuntimeID is the runtime profile the caller prefers, as listed by
GET /runtimes. It must name an existing profile.

targetNodes.description: TargetNodes are the nodes the model is meant to run on, at most 32.

tasks.description:
Tasks are what the model is to be used for, in the words of the catalog
tasks[]: chat, vision-chat or embedding.

candidates.description:
Candidates are ordered best first. Empty means nothing in the catalog
fits.

recommender.description:
Recommender is the name of the implementation that answered, as set in
AIAPP_RECOMMENDER_MODEL.

infraId.description: InfraID is the CB-Tumblebug Infra the node belongs to.

nodeId.description: NodeID is the node within the Infra. It needs infraId.

nsId.description: NsID is the CB-Tumblebug namespace of the Infra.

BearerAuth.description: "Bearer <token>". Required on every route but readiness, the console and this documentation when AIAPP_AUTH_TOKEN is set.
BearerAuth.name: Authorization
